page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-4 is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. Built on the Intel Xeon x86_64 platform, each core supports two hardware threads and incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache pool. Advanced instruction support includes AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic AES extensions. The machine provides 4.0 GB of total RAM, yielding an allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU. No local solid-state drives or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, meaning all persistent file systems must rely on external network storage.

Synthetic benchmark results place the n2-highcpu-4 primarily in the lower quartile across general-purpose execution metrics. In Geekbench testing, the server attained 1156.0 points in single-core and 2529.0 points in multi-core evaluation, alongside a Clang compilation score of 3497.0. PassMark evaluation demonstrated a CPU score of 4324.89 and a memory rating of 1052.97. Uncached memory bandwidth measured 27.14 GB/sec for reads and 22.64 GB/sec for writes. The instance sustained 3.65 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 4.05 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 8.97 GB/sec, representing its strongest comparative result.

The primary operational constraint of the n2-highcpu-4 is its restricted memory capacity relative to core count. At 1.0 GB per vCPU, memory-intensive jobs risk resource exhaustion, making this server unsuitable for large in-memory databases or caching layers. However, from a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, dedicating resources predominantly to compute cycles allows deployments to avoid paying for excess RAM. The instance fits lightweight batch jobs, distributed CI/CD build agents, task queue processing, and CPU-bound stateless microservices where operational memory footprints remain under 4 GB.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-4 is a compute-oriented virtual machine providing 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 33 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and VNNI vector instruction extensions. The instance comes without bundled local storage and includes no discrete GPUs, necessitating external network-attached block volumes for state persistence. In performance testing, the instance registers entry-tier throughput across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng benchmarks, reflecting its modest 4-thread execution envelope. Memory throughput is constrained by the 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and PassMark memory benchmarks fall within the bottom tier. Given the high-CPU to low-memory ratio and baseline performance characteristics, the n2-highcpu-4 provides qualitative cost efficiency for batch processing, lightweight background worker services, source compilation queues, and stateless microservices with minimal RAM footprints.
